summary: Full RBAC review for iteration 22 (staff roles & permissions). Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iteration22_rbac.py (24 tests, all passing) covering /auth/me permission payload, /admin/permissions catalogue + gating, /admin/team CRUD guardrails (self edit, invalid status, empty body, unknown/malformed id, scope mismatch, duplicate email, over-grant), the exact 200/403 matrix for the perm.test moderator + payouts:view account, per-role matrices for finance/support/viewer, moderator lockout from /admin/verifications, console permission split for vendor_viewer (read-only) vs vendor_manager (writes work when active, 403 with pending message when status=pending), and full admin + legacy manager regression across all control-centre and console endpoints. Playwright verified the Admin tabs are filtered for perm.test (dashboard/team/settings hidden, first available tab auto-selected), the admin 'Team & roles' tab exposes team-panel with invite form (team-name/email/scope/role/perm-* checkboxes/invite-btn), team-table renders team-row-<id> with team-edit/team-status/team-perms testids, preset permissions come pre-checked+disabled (moderator preset locks moderation:manage), permissions the caller lacks are disabled (admin caller can enable team:manage), the mobile 390px view renders the panel cleanly with no overflow, and ops.manager sees console-tab-invites (legacy manager still holds invites:manage).
critical_code_review_comments: Team.jsx: editing a team-row's staff_role via the inline select fires save() with extra_permissions=[] on every change event. That is documented as 'preset only' behaviour, but users might accidentally lose extras they had — consider a Confirm/Save button so edits are explicit.

Admin.jsx NAV filter uses `perms.length === 0 || perms.includes(p)` which means a legacy account whose /auth/me hasn't loaded yet briefly renders ALL tabs (including team) before permissions arrive. Not a security issue (backend enforces), but a fleeting UI flash. Consider hiding until user is resolved.

server.py suspension guardrail (`Keep at least one active super admin`) counts docs with staff_role in ['super_admin', None, '']; the legacy admin@buddilio.com has no staff_role so it counts correctly today, but the moment a super_admin is explicitly promoted, unrelated legacy admins keep the count above 1 and the guard may pass even when only they remain — worth revisiting once every account is migrated onto a staff_role.
